newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie leaves jail for first day of work.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie leaves jail for first day of work.

text.p: Fallen French tycoon Bernard Tapie left prison on Tuesday for his first day of work under a programme granting him freedom during the day as long as he returns to his cell at night, a prison source said.
He will be a business associate at Secna, a naval construction firm run by his long-time friend Michel Bigoin, who renovated Tapie's majestic four-masted yacht in 1986.
Tapie's use of the yacht earned him a prison sentence for tax evasion after he tried to pass off its costs as a business expense.

Tapie must be back in his cell at Marseile's Baumettes jail by 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) each night of the six-month contract with Secna during which he will be charged with drumming up new business for the company.
He will have to take a two-week holiday from the job from May 12 to May 30 as he stands trial again, this time over charges of fraud in the management of the OM Marseille soccer side.
